title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025

claims.claim: For decades, families of Holocaust victims have tried to recover artwork stolen by Nazi Germany.
claims.sourceSpan: artwork or other property lost during the covered period because, or as a result, of Nazi persecution
claims.note: 'for decades'/'families' is background framing consistent with source's Nazi-persecution scope.

claims.claim: American courts have dismissed these cases on procedural grounds - time delays, deference to foreign governments, or doctrines unrelated to who actually owned the art.
claims.sourceSpan: Some courts have frustrated the intent of this Act by dismissing recovery lawsuits in reliance on defenses based on the passage of time, such as laches
claims.note: 'deference to foreign governments' = gloss on act of state / international comity.

claims.claim: This law permanently removes those barriers.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim
claims.note: 'permanently' supported: 5(f) carries no sunset and the Dec 31 2026 sunset is removed.

claims.claim: It prohibits courts from dismissing Holocaust art claims based on the passage of time or other procedural defenses.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim

claims.claim: It strips foreign governments of a key immunity argument regardless of the victim's nationality.
claims.sourceSpan: any civil claim or cause of action covered by subsection (a) shall be deemed to be an action in which rights in violation of international law are in issue for purposes of section 1605(a)(3) of title 28, United States Code, without regard to the nationality or citizenship of the alleged victim

claims.claim: It removes the December 31, 2026 filing deadline entirely.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026
claims.note: Dec 31 2026 figure from referenced 2016 Act; amendment strikes the dated window and inserts 'on or after the date of enactment'.

claims.claim: It applies all of those changes retroactively to cases currently in court.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to any civil claim or cause of action that is-- (1) pending in any court on the date of enactment of this Act, including any civil claim or cause of action that is pending on appeal or for which the time to file an appeal has not expired

claims.claim: Permanently bars courts from dismissing Nazi-looted art claims on procedural grounds.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim

claims.claim: Overrides multiple appellate and Supreme Court rulings that had blocked recovery.
claims.sourceSpan: Some courts have frustrated the intent of this Act by dismissing recovery lawsuits in reliance on defenses based on the passage of time, such as laches
claims.note: Appellate: Zuckerman (2d Cir), Cassirer (9th Cir), Von Saher (9th Cir); Supreme Court: Philipp (see 592 U.S. 169 (2021)).

claims.claim: Procedural Defenses Eliminated.
claims.sourceSpan: all non-merits discretionary bases for dismissal, including the act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, prudential exhaustion, and similar doctrines unrelated to the merits, may not be applied with respect to the claim

claims.claim: Laches, adverse possession, international comity, forum non conveniens, and act of state doctrine may no longer be used to dismiss Holocaust art claims.
claims.sourceSpan: all non-merits discretionary bases for dismissal, including the act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, prudential exhaustion, and similar doctrines unrelated to the merits, may not be applied with respect to the claim
claims.note: Laches/adverse possession appear in 5(f)(1); act of state/comity/forum non conveniens in 5(f)(2).

claims.claim: Applies retroactively to cases currently pending, including those on appeal.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to any civil claim or cause of action that is-- (1) pending in any court on the date of enactment of this Act, including any civil claim or cause of action that is pending on appeal or for which the time to file an appeal has not expired

claims.claim: Foreign Sovereign Immunity Overridden.
claims.sourceSpan: any civil claim or cause of action covered by subsection (a) shall be deemed to be an action in which rights in violation of international law are in issue for purposes of section 1605(a)(3) of title 28, United States Code, without regard to the nationality or citizenship of the alleged victim

claims.claim: Claims against foreign governments proceed regardless of victim nationality - overrides the 2021 Supreme Court ruling in Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp.
claims.sourceSpan: under Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp, 592 U.S. 169
claims.note: '2021' and 'Supreme Court' from citation '592 U.S. 169 (2021)'.

claims.claim: Nationwide service of process added, allowing courts to reach defendants in any U.S. district.
claims.sourceSpan: For a civil action brought under subsection (a) in any State or Federal court, process may be served in the judicial district where the case is brought or any other judicial district of the United States where the defendant may be found, resides, has an agent, or transacts business
claims.note: Source qualifies 'any district' by where the defendant is found, resides, has an agent, or transacts business.

claims.claim: Filing Deadline Removed.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026

claims.claim: December 31, 2026 filing deadline eliminated - claims may be filed at any time.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026
claims.note: 'at any time' = open-ended window; amendment inserts 'on or after the date of enactment'.

claims.claim: Six-year discovery period from the date the claimant learns of the artwork's location still applies.
claims.sourceSpan: may be commenced not later than 6 years after the actual discovery by the claimant
claims.note: Amendment does not touch subsection (a) discovery rule; 'location' per 5(a)(1).

claims.claim: Signed into law by the President on April 13, 2026.
claims.sourceSpan: Approved April 13, 2026
claims.note: 'Approved April 13, 2026' = presidential approval date.

claims.claim: Enacted as Public Law 119-82.
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-82

claims.claim: Names the Act the 'Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025'; short-title section, no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the
claims.note: Title citation only.

claims.claim: Adds new Section 5(f) to the HEAR Act of 2016, barring all time-based defenses and all non-merits discretionary bases for dismissal against otherwise timely Holocaust art claims.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim
claims.note: 'otherwise timely' verbatim in 5(f).

claims.claim: Prohibited time-based defenses include laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim

claims.claim: Prohibited non-merits defenses include the act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, and prudential exhaustion.
claims.sourceSpan: all non-merits discretionary bases for dismissal, including the act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, prudential exhaustion, and similar doctrines unrelated to the merits, may not be applied with respect to the claim

claims.claim: The bill adds findings naming Zuckerman v. Metropolitan Museum of Art (2d Cir. 2019).
claims.sourceSpan: Zuckerman v Metropolitan Museum of Art, 928 F.3d 186 (2d Cir. 2019)

claims.claim: The bill adds findings naming Cassirer v. Thyssen-Bornemisza Foundation (9th Cir. 2024).
claims.sourceSpan: Cassirer v. Thyssen-Bornemisza Foundation, 89 F.4th 1226 (9th Cir. 2024)

claims.claim: The bill adds findings naming Von Saher v. Norton Simon Museum of Art (9th Cir. 2018).
claims.sourceSpan: Von Saher v Norton Simon Museum of Art at Pasadena, 897 F.3d 1141 (9th Cir. 2018)

claims.claim: New Section 5(b) deems Holocaust art claims to constitute actions involving violations of international law for purposes of the FSIA (28 U.S.C. 1605(a)(3)), regardless of the nationality or citizenship of the alleged victim.
claims.sourceSpan: any civil claim or cause of action covered by subsection (a) shall be deemed to be an action in which rights in violation of international law are in issue for purposes of section 1605(a)(3) of title 28, United States Code, without regard to the nationality or citizenship of the alleged victim
claims.note: FSIA framing supported by subsection header 'Relation to Foreign State Immunities'.

claims.claim: This directly overrides Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp, 592 U.S. 169 (2021).
claims.sourceSpan: under Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp, 592 U.S. 169

claims.claim: In Philipp the Supreme Court held that the 'domestic takings' rule barred FSIA jurisdiction over property seized from a country's own nationals.
claims.sourceSpan: under Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp, 592 U.S. 169
claims.note: Extrinsic characterization of the Philipp holding; source names the 'domestic takings' rule but does not state what it held. Consistent with source's 'regardless of nationality' framing but not source-stated.

claims.claim: Nationwide service of process is added for all civil actions under the Act.
claims.sourceSpan: For a civil action brought under subsection (a) in any State or Federal court, process may be served in the judicial district where the case is brought or any other judicial district of the United States where the defendant may be found, resides, has an agent, or transacts business
claims.note: Source scopes service to a civil action brought under subsection (a).

claims.claim: All amendments apply to claims pending on the date of enactment (including cases pending on appeal or within the appeal filing window) and to cases filed after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to any civil claim or cause of action that is-- (1) pending in any court on the date of enactment of this Act, including any civil claim or cause of action that is pending on appeal or for which the time to file an appeal has not expired
claims.note: Post-enactment prong: 'filed on or after the date of enactment of this Act'.

claims.claim: Removes the December 31, 2026 deadline for filing claims and replaces it with a perpetual filing window subject to a six-year discovery period.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026
claims.section: ref S.2763 sec 5(c)(1)(B) / amend sec 2(a)(3)(F) / sec 5(a)
claims.note: 'perpetual window' = removal of the dated sunset; amendment inserts 'on or after the date of enactment'; six-year rule from 5(a).

claims.claim: Under prior law, all claims had to be filed by December 31, 2026 regardless of when the claimant discovered the property's location.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026
claims.note: Dec 31 2026 was the outer applicability/filing window in the referenced 2016 Act.

claims.claim: This deadline is eliminated.
claims.sourceSpan: and all that follows and inserting
claims.note: Strikes 'during the period' and all that follows; inserts 'on or after the date of enactment'.

claims.claim: Claims must still be filed within six years of the claimant's discovery of the property in question.
claims.sourceSpan: may be commenced not later than 6 years after the actual discovery by the claimant

claims.claim: Section 5(b) - FSIA exception: Holocaust art claims deemed violations of international law under 28 U.S.C. 1605(a)(3) regardless of victim nationality.
claims.sourceSpan: any civil claim or cause of action covered by subsection (a) shall be deemed to be an action in which rights in violation of international law are in issue for purposes of section 1605(a)(3) of title 28, United States Code, without regard to the nationality or citizenship of the alleged victim

claims.claim: Section 5(f) - prohibition on all time-based defenses (laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, usucapion) and non-merits discretionary defenses (act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, prudential exhaustion).
claims.sourceSpan: all non-merits discretionary bases for dismissal, including the act of state doctrine, international comity, forum non conveniens, prudential exhaustion, and similar doctrines unrelated to the merits, may not be applied with respect to the claim
claims.note: Time-based list in 5(f)(1); non-merits list in 5(f)(2).

claims.claim: Section 5(g) - nationwide service of process for Holocaust art civil actions.
claims.sourceSpan: For a civil action brought under subsection (a) in any State or Federal court, process may be served in the judicial district where the case is brought or any other judicial district of the United States where the defendant may be found, resides, has an agent, or transacts business

claims.claim: Section 6 - severability provision.
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 6. SEVERABILITY.

claims.claim: HEAR Act of 2016 findings expanded to name specific court decisions that frustrated the Act's intent and to state that non-merits defenses must be precluded.
claims.sourceSpan: these defenses must be precluded
claims.note: Named cases and 'these defenses must be precluded' both in new finding (8).

claims.claim: HEAR Act Section 3(2) - definition of covered defenses expanded to include 'and other non-merits defenses' alongside statutes of limitation.
claims.sourceSpan: in section 3(2), by inserting
claims.note: Insertion is real; label 'definition' is imprecise - in the referenced text section 3(2) is a Purposes clause, not a definition.

claims.claim: December 31, 2026 filing deadline for Holocaust art recovery claims removed.
claims.sourceSpan: filed during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2026

claims.claim: The law applies to any civil claim pending in any court on the date of enactment, including claims pending on appeal and claims for which the time to file an appeal has not yet expired.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to any civil claim or cause of action that is-- (1) pending in any court on the date of enactment of this Act, including any civil claim or cause of action that is pending on appeal or for which the time to file an appeal has not expired

claims.claim: Courts that previously dismissed Holocaust art claims on laches or international comity grounds could have those dismissals challenged or reversed under the new law.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to any civil claim or cause of action that is-- (1) pending in any court on the date of enactment of this Act, including any civil claim or cause of action that is pending on appeal or for which the time to file an appeal has not expired
claims.note: Analytical inference about litigation effect; applicability clause reaches pending/appealed claims but the source does not state dismissals will be reversed.

claims.claim: The law bars procedural defenses but does not address the evidentiary standard for establishing provenance or Nazi-era confiscation in the underlying merits of a claim.
claims.sourceSpan: all defenses or substantive doctrines based on the passage of time, including laches, adverse possession, acquisitive prescription, and usucapion, may not be applied with respect to the claim
claims.note: True negative: bill governs defenses/timeliness; neither source sets a provenance/merits evidentiary standard.

claims.claim: The law covers artwork lost 'because, or as a result, of Nazi persecution.'
claims.sourceSpan: artwork or other property lost during the covered period because, or as a result, of Nazi persecution

claims.claim: The law does not address property transferred through forced sales under economic duress rather than outright confiscation.
claims.sourceSpan: includes any theft, seizure, forced sale, sale under duress, or any other loss of an artwork or cultural property that would not have occurred absent persecution during the Nazi era
claims.section: ref S.2763 sec 4(4) definition of 'unlawfully lost'
claims.note: Contradicted: the referenced 2016 Act (unchanged by this bill) defines 'unlawfully lost' to expressly INCLUDE 'forced sale, sale under duress.' Forced sales under duress ARE covered, so this is not a gap; the claim misleads readers into thinking such victims are excluded.

claims.claim: The bill also softens the HEAR Act's own findings: it strikes 'will yield just and fair resolutions in a more efficient and predictable manner' and inserts 'may, in some circumstances, yield just and fair resolutions as well' - a material tempering of the original Act's stated expectation that the analysis does not mention.
claims.sourceSpan: may, in some circumstances, yield just and fair resolutions as well
claims.note: Substantive findings edit present in source (strikes 'will yield just and fair resolutions in a more efficient and predictable manner') but absent from the analysis's changes/sections.

notes: Source-only hostile pass. Evidence = data/bill-text/119-S-1884.txt (Public Law 119-82) plus registered referencedSource data/ref-text/bill-114-s-2763.txt (introduced 2016 HEAR Act; only the introduced version is in-evidence, so figures such as the Dec 31 2026 window and the 6-year discovery rule and the 'unlawfully lost' definition are judged against it). featured_quotes are Congressional Record floor statements (Raskin, Lee) not present in either source file, so they were not source-verifiable in this pass and are not recorded as claim rows. One material issue: gaps[1] asserts forced sales under duress are not addressed, but the referenced Act's definition of 'unlawfully lost' expressly includes 'forced sale, sale under duress.'
